thesis: A dispatch desk that had become the county's default number for everything bought one voice workflow, pointed it at the routine line only, and left the line where a wrong answer hurts somebody completely alone.
_thesis_note: The deck's one idea is the BOUNDARY, not the machine. Everything good here follows from where the line got drawn, and the Ozaukee beat is structural proof rather than a disclaimer, because the same product went sideways sixty miles away when somebody drew it too wide.

vocabulary_lock.the_line: Called 'the routine line' on every slide. The precise phrase 'non-emergency line' appears exactly ONCE, on slide 4, where the mechanism is defined.
vocabulary_lock.the_system: Called 'the voice workflow' or 'Ava'. Never 'the AI'.
vocabulary_lock.the_desk: Called 'the desk' or 'the dispatch desk'. The word 'county' never appears in a headline position.
vocabulary_lock.units: Calls, always. Never minutes, never hours, never tickets.

hard_copy_rules: The string '105,000' appears on exactly ONE slide (2). The string '65 percent' appears on exactly ONE slide (6). NO slide contains both, and no slide performs or implies arithmetic between them. Machine-greppable and it will be grepped.
The 65 percent always travels with its base and its verb in the same breath: it is a share of the 41,000 calls the system TOOK, and it counts calls that ENDED, not calls that got ANSWERED.
'Approximate to one employee with benefits' is attributed to Milwaukee Magazine in the same breath, every time. It is never put in Cory Lynch's mouth or the county's.

The timeline is only ever 'several months of training before it took its first call on 5 May 2025'. Never 'several months from decision to working'. Spokane's six weeks is off limits under any framing because it is a different vendor.
No freed hour is ever converted into a dollar. They kept all four dispatchers per shift.
The Ozaukee beat always carries the vendor-receptive clause. Cutting it makes the slide a hit piece and an inaccurate one.

slides.promise: That question is landing on the same desk that answers 911, and something concrete happened about it
A desk with four people on it and six seats it cannot fill is taking a hundred thousand of those a year, so what happens when the wrong one lands
This is what it costs when the real call arrives mid-conversation, so what did they actually do about it
They rebuilt one line and left the other untouched, and step four says escalate on a word, so which words and who chose them
The gate is a list a person typed, which means the machine is matching words rather than judging urgency, so how much of the load actually moved
It moved a lot, and one outcome nobody has ever published, so does it work like this everywhere it is bought
It does not, and the difference was where the boundary went, so what would I actually be signing up for
A price that rises as it works, a ramp with no start date on the record, and an owner who runs the desk, so where does my own boundary go
Here is the line to point it at, the harder local version of what broke Ozaukee, and the cheaper answer if your volume is small
